title: implement-offline-bundle-signing-and-ubuntu-focal-runtime-support
author: Aditi Shah
description:
Context: Customers running the Private (on-prem / air-gapped) installer reported two recurring requirements: (1) the ability to verify vendor bundles with cryptographic signatures before install to satisfy security/compliance policies, and (2) out-of-the-box runtime artifacts that match Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (focal) node images used by several enterprise customers. This PR implements signed offline bundles plus vendored .deb runtime packages and adds installer-side verification + a documented key rotation flow.

Summary of changes: add GPG signing workflow for generated airgap bundles, include a minimal set of Ubuntu Focal .deb runtime artifacts (glibc/backports + kernel-headers pinned), verify signatures during preflight, extend the installer CLI to accept a --trusted-keys path or use the built-in bundle keyring, and add a rollback-safe unpack path when signature checks fail. Also includes documentation for operators (key rotation, emergency revoke) and CI coverage for signature verification.

Checklist:
- [x] Add signing key generation and verification helpers
- [x] Vendor focal runtime .deb artifacts and metadata in slim bundle variant
- [x] Installer preflight verifies signature and package checksums
- [x] CLI flag --trusted-keys and key rotation docs
- [x] Integration test that exercises an unsigned-bundle failure and a successful signed-bundle path
- [x] Release notes and upgrade guidance

Why this approach: Signing bundles gives a minimal, auditable trust boundary for air-gapped installs without requiring an external KMS. Vendor .deb artifacts for focal are limited to runtime packages that customers commonly lock on (libc, udev, iproute2) to reduce drift between the runtime the installer configures and customer node OS. The verification happens pre-extract so we avoid partially-applied installs and preserve rollback semantics.

Related: builds on some prework in ENG-8320 (airgap bundle refactor), and addresses SUP-1286 customer asks about offline verification.

merge_commit_message:
squash: add offline bundle signing and Ubuntu Focal runtime artifacts

Signed-off-by: Aditi Shah
release_notes:
- Added cryptographic signing for airgap/offline bundles. Installer now verifies bundle signatures and checksums before extraction.
- Vendor-matched runtime packages for Ubuntu 20.04 (focal) included in slim bundle variant to reduce OS drift for customers on focal.
- New CLI flag --trusted-keys and operator docs for key rotation and emergency revoke.
upgrade_notes: Operator guidance: existing airgap bundles are still supported. To use signing, generate or import a signing key and populate --trusted-keys before running install. See docs/airgap/signing-keys.md for command examples. No automatic migration is performed; operators must coordinate key rollout across nodes.
notes_for_release_manager: This PR touches offline bundles and the slim runtime set. Validate installation on Ubuntu 20.04 testbeds and ensure the signed-bundle verification is part of the release smoke test. Coordinate with the SRE team before enabling signed-bundle enforcement by default.
post_merge_actions: Publish public bundle signing key to customer portal
Add signed-bundle verification to release smoke CI
